title: Carapace Capability Taxonomy
description: Controlled vocabulary of agent capability scopes for the Carapace Protocol. Version 0.1.0. Capability IDs in this taxonomy are machine-readable, hierarchical, and carry defined permission implications. Free-text capability IDs are still permitted but will not receive automated scope enforcement.

carapace.description: Official Carapace capability namespace. Maintained by RelayForge.

read.description: Read-only access to external resources. No mutations, no side effects.

carapace:read:web.description: Fetch publicly accessible web content via HTTP/HTTPS GET.

carapace:read:filesystem.description: Read files from a defined path scope on the host filesystem.

carapace:read:database.description: Execute read-only queries against a database.

carapace:read:email.description: Read email messages from a mailbox.

carapace:read:memory.description: Read from agent long-term memory or vector store.

write.description: Mutating access. Creates, modifies, or deletes external state.

carapace:write:filesystem.description: Write, create, or modify files within a declared path scope.

carapace:write:database.description: Execute write operations against a database (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).

carapace:write:calendar.description: Create, modify, or delete calendar events.

carapace:write:memory.description: Write to agent long-term memory or vector store.

execute.description: Execution capabilities. Highest privilege tier — requires explicit justification.

carapace:execute:shell.description: Execute shell commands on the host system.
carapace:execute:shell.side_effects: arbitrary — treat as unrestricted system access

carapace:execute:code.description: Execute arbitrary code in a sandboxed runtime.

carapace:execute:api.description: Call external APIs with side-effectful operations (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH).

carapace:execute:process_control.description: Interact with industrial control systems, PLCs, SCADA, or OT environments.
carapace:execute:process_control.notes: Industrial use only. Requires ISA/IEC 62443 alignment attestation.

carapace:communicate:a2a.description: Send tasks or messages to other A2A-registered agents.

carapace:communicate:mcp.description: Call tools exposed via MCP servers.

carapace:communicate:human.description: Send messages, notifications, or alerts to human operators.

observe.description: Monitoring and telemetry capabilities. Read-only but continuous.

carapace:observe:logs.description: Read system, application, or audit logs.

carapace:observe:metrics.description: Read system or application performance metrics.

examples: Reading pressure, flow, temperature from DCS

risk_levels.low: No external side effects. Read-only or sandboxed.
risk_levels.medium: External reads or minor persistent writes. Reversible in most cases.
risk_levels.high: Persistent external mutations. Hard to reverse.
risk_levels.critical: Physical effects, unrestricted execution, or safety-system interaction.

scope_declaration.description: Capabilities marked requires_scope_declaration must include a scope object in the capability definition specifying which resources the agent is authorized to access.

attestation_requirement.description: Capabilities marked requires_attestation must carry a signed third-party attestation in the agent card before the capability is considered credentialed (vs. merely declared).

versioning.policy: Capability IDs are stable once published. New scopes are additive. Deprecated scopes are marked deprecated for two minor versions before removal. Breaking changes require a major version bump and advance notice.
versioning.stability: draft — open for community feedback before 1.0.0 freeze

contributing.description: To propose a new capability scope, open an issue at github.com/relayforge/carapace-protocol with the prefix 'Taxonomy:'. Include: proposed ID, description, side effects, data sensitivity, reversibility, and at least two real-world use cases.
contributing.governance: RelayForge maintains the carapace: namespace. Third parties may define their own namespaces using reverse-domain notation (e.g., com.acme:read:proprietary-system).
